on_screen: Title card: Danza de los Diablos (Diablada) · Bolivia · 18th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is believed to have originated 2000 years ago as the Llama llama ritual of the Uru civilization in Oruro.
During the colonial era, Spanish authorities banned indigenous ceremonies, leading the Uru to conceal their gods behind Christian icons.
The god Tiw was transformed into 'El Tío' and the devil of Christian liturgy.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is the centerpiece of the Carnaval de Oruro and the Fiesta de la Candelaria.
It represents the struggle between good and evil, the Seven Deadly Sins, and the syncretic relationship between miners and the spirits of the underworld.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is a series of three versions, each consisting of seven moves.
It features a confrontation between angels and demons who move continuously in formations like circles and crosses.
Demons perform 'kick jumps' (pieds sautés) while the Archangel uses a sword and shield to direct the troop.
Watch for Pieds sautés.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Linear columns, circular rotations, and intersecting crosses in public squares.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Originally performed with Sikuris (panpipe bands), modern versions use brass orchestras.
The music consists of two parts: the March and the Devil's Mecapaqueña.
Listen for the Siku, Bass drum, Snare drum, Cymbals.
A powerful brass-heavy sound characterized by crashing cymbals and driving percussion, transitioning from a formal military-style march to a faster, syncopated Andean rhythm.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers wear monstrous masks with horns and bulging eyes, and heavy capes embroidered with gold thread and multicolored motifs.
The Archangel wears a blouse, short skirt, and wings.
Settings range from the streets and public squares of Oruro and Puno to indoor theaters.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Pedro Pablo Corrales founded the first formal squad in 1904.
The Archangel Saint Michael is the lead character, while Lucifer and Satan lead the demonic ranks.
The Diablada Puneña (Peru) includes characters like the 'Old Man' and 'Red Skin' and was influenced by Jesuit autos sacramentales.
Descended from the Uru Llama llama and Aymara rituals to Anchanchu.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Danza de los Diablos (Diablada) is influence of Tinku: Some theories suggest the Diablada originated from miners combining Tinku rituals with Christian icons.
Danza de los Diablos (Diablada) is same region of Morenada: Another major dance of the Carnaval de Oruro sharing the same syncretic history.
